_doc: Reusable rule components — the shelf a client picks from.
A client file references one by name instead of restating its body:
"use": [
"paneer_once_a_week",
{"ref": "selector_once_a_week", "as": "acme_mushroom_1x",
"with": {"selector": {"primary_protein": "mushroom"}}}
A bare string uses the component as-is and takes its name. The object form
renames it (`as`) and shallow-merges `with` over the template per key, the
same semantics client rules already use to override a city rule — so a
component covers a family of requirements without a templating language.
This exists because the same body was copy-pasted across clients: 'paneer
once a week' appeared verbatim in ELEVEN client files, 'mushroom once a
week' in four, 'plain chapati twice a week' in three. Each copy is a place
the wording can drift, and a fix to one is a fix to one.
A component is only worth adding when a SECOND client needs it. One client
with an unusual requirement writes an ordinary rule in its own file.

paneer_once_a_week._doc: Exactly one paneer dish across the week, anywhere on the counter.

paneer_twice_a_week._doc: Exactly two paneer dishes across the week.

_doc: Exactly one dish of some family across the week. Override `selector`
(and `base_slot` to scope it) — used for mushroom, baby corn, soya.
A family may appear on at most N days a week. Override `selector` and
`max`; add `base_slot` to scope it to one station.
The Indian bread slot is a chapati or phulka, every day.
A one-slot `slot_composition` component IS 'this slot must be a matching
dish' (CLAUDE.md note 20) — `fixed_daily_item` is the wrong tool, it only
makes the dish CONSISTENT and leaves the solver free to serve something
else. Self-gates on a single-bread counter.
Selects on the FLAG, not on the name. It used to match `name_contains:
[chapati, chapatti, phulka]`, which is what the flag being unreliable
forced — and the cost showed up the moment Citrix was wired: Tuesday's
'chapati' came back `appam_chapati`, a combination cell a menu import
split badly. `scripts/bread_form_flags.py` made the flag definitional in
both directions (a competing bread form in the name clears it), so the
column is now the trustworthy selector and the name is the blunt one.

plain_chapati_twice_a_week._doc: Plain chapati/phulka on exactly two days; other days vary.

_doc: Plain chapati may run on consecutive days — it is a staple, not a
variety slot. Needed by any client that pins or mandates it daily:
without the declaration `unique_items` forbids the repeat and the
counter goes INFEASIBLE (CLAUDE.md note 18).
On the Chinese day the veg dry is a regular north or south Indian dish,
not a manchurian — the themed veg is the gravy. Both regions stay in the
pool so the objective picks whichever suits the day.
indian_veg_dry_on_chinese_day.name: theme_cuisine_filter

_doc: The non-veg station runs only on the listed weekdays. Override
`allowed_weekdays` (lowercase 3-letter names).

egg_dish_once_a_week._doc: Exactly one egg dish in the non-veg slot across the week.

pulao_three_days_a_week._doc: Exactly three pulao days in the flavoured-rice slot.

_doc: At least one dish a day whose key_ingredient is a protein source, from
flavoured rice / veg gravy / veg dry / salad / dal. `daily_min` (not
`min`) so it means EVERY day whatever the horizon length.
The protein must not always be the dal: at least 3 days carry one from
rice / veg gravy / veg dry / salad. Pair with
`protein_outside_dal_other_days` for the remaining days.
Soft companion to the floor above: take the remaining days too whenever
no other rule has to give. A hard every-day floor would trade a whole
plan for one dish.
The non-veg station serves chicken only — no egg, mutton or fish.
Expressed as a ban on the others rather than a chicken mandate, so a day
the station is off is not forced to carry one.

curd_rice_once_a_week._doc: Curd rice appears on exactly one day in the healthy-rice slot.

nonveg_dry_once_a_week._doc: One dry (non-gravy) non-veg dish across the week.
